title: Slimdown routing slowpath and migrate to policy-v2
creator: Ava Chen
description:
Summary: Reduce long-tail latency and simplify the smart-routing slowpath by migrating the legacy policy engine to the policy-v2 runtime, pruning legacy routing branches, and removing a set of ad-hoc regional locks. This ticket covers the code migration, dependency upgrades needed for policy-v2, and a targeted set of micro-optimizations to eliminate an observed 95th/99th token latency regression in cross-region failovers.

Motivation: Over the last year we've accumulated multiple small fallback branches and a compatibility shim between policy-v1 and newer routing adapters. Those additions increase cognitive overhead, introduce global mutexes under surge, and make incremental improvements risky. Customers on Dedicated have reported bursty latency during regional failover scenarios; internal traces point to slowpath state reconciliation and contention in the legacy evaluator.

Goals:
- Replace runtime calls to policy-v1 with policy-v2 adapter (backwards-compatible façade)
- Remove three legacy fallback branches that are unused by current routing configs (identified in routing-audit-2025 Q2)
- Replace global shard locks with per-region admission tokens and non-blocking lease allocator
- Upgrade protobuf (v3.18 -> v3.21) and grpc (v1.47 -> v1.52) to satisfy policy-v2 SDK; audit generated stubs
- Measure and reduce 95th/99th latency by >= 25% on cross-region failover benchmarks

Out-of-scope: Full rewrite of router hotpath, UI changes in Console, changes to routing policy DSL semantics. This ticket keeps existing policy semantics intact via adapter.

Acceptance criteria: See acceptance_criteria field.

acceptance_criteria: policy-v2 adapter merged and toggled behind feature flag (route.policy_v2=true)
No behavior changes for existing routes when feature flag is off (integration test suite passing)
95th/99th cross-region failover latency reduced by >=25% in benchmark harness compared to baseline (measured over 24h)
Global routing mutex removed and replaced with per-region lease allocator, verified by code inspect and stress test
Protobuf/grpc upgrade merged and dependency graph updated; CI green for linux/arm64 and container image builds
PRs reviewed by infra (Ben K.) and research (Priya M.) and approved
Migration runbook created and rollback plan validated in staging
implementation_notes: Introduce policy-v2 adapter layer under routing/adapters/policy_v2_adapter.go; adapter preserves policy-v1 call signatures until toggle is flipped
Extract legacy slowpath reconciliation into routing/slowpath/legacy_reconcile.go and mark for removal after migration window
Implement non-blocking lease allocator using lock-free queues; keep metrics for lease_acquire_latency{region} and lease_contention_count
Update buf.gen.yaml and regenerate protobuf stubs; run go mod tidy and validate module graph does not pull old grpc versions
Add feature flag gating and a gradual rollout: 5% -> 25% -> 100% with observability checks at each step
Add unit tests for adapter, plus end-to-end integration tests covering failover and canary traffic paths
testing_plan: Unit: adapter compatibility tests for existing policy rules
Integration: full routing suite with simulated regional outage (baseline vs policy-v2) in CI park
Staging soak: 48h canary with 10% of production traffic using policy_v2 flag, monitor latency/error rates
Chaos: inject region-partition and validate graceful degrade and fallback correctness
Benchmark: run cross-region token-generation harness (100k requests) and collect p50/p95/p99 and token-cost metrics
rollback_plan: Keep feature flag switch to revert to policy-v1; if protobuf incompatibility found, revert dependency merge and publish emergency compatibility patch. If performance regressions >10% occur after 25% rollout, pause rollout, revert flag and run postmortem.
